findings.claim: Endpoint-integrated shape contrasts are the strongest signed coordinate signals: shape_yy shows a negative high-low integrated z with zero positive batches and a small q, and shape_xx is similarly negative with a small q; both are absolute geometric descriptors of the endpoint pointcloud, not selection enrichment.

Global centroid_y shows a negative high-low integrated z with a small q and low positive-batch fraction, while centroid_x and centroid_z are not distinguishable from zero; the centroid shift is a population-level contrast, not a per-node selection effect.

Continuous landmark features over the observed window are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dx/dy/dz show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts with no accepted polynomial, so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must be validated at observed nodes only.

The observed window is the learning window [0.0,0.5] with score times on a 0.01 grid and curve support [0.0,0.49]; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior is used, so no final-affinity benefit can be read from these coordinate contrasts.

hypotheses.direction: increase magnitude of negative shape_yy/shape_xx endpoint contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: no change or opposite-sign shift in endpoint-integrated shape_yy/shape_xx contrast relative to the static rule at matched batches
hypotheses.observable: endpoint-integrated shape_yy and shape_xx high-low z
hypotheses.scope: observed score window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention rule keyed to validated landmark contrast changes at observed score nodes will produce a larger signed endpoint shape_yy/shape_xx contrast than a constant static-teacher rule.

hypotheses.direction: more negative centroid_y high-low integrated contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: centroid_y contrast unchanged or centroid_x/centroid_z contrast changes comparably
hypotheses.scope: observed score window, predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A centroid_y-directed coordinate contrast at observed selection nodes will shift the endpoint centroid_y contrast without altering centroid_x or centroid_z.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final-affinity outcomes are supplied; last-record and survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Continuous trend fits are observed-node linear with no accepted polynomial and no extrapolation; time-conditioned claims are restricted to the observed window.
Turnover, increment and survival tables were not read in this budget; within-path change versus cohort composition remains unassessed.
Contrast curves are coordinate rewards, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies.
